target.title: fix(ios): render Markdown lists and thematic breaks
target.body: Closes #104548 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where iOS users reading an agent response with Markdown lists would see list markers and item boundaries flattened into generic prose. The same path also left thematic breaks as literal Markdown instead of visual separators. This made structured answers harder to scan, especially for nested steps, task lists, and ordered choices. ## Why This Change Was Made Completed top-level ordered, unordered, and task lists now render through a bounded native SwiftUI block while preserving nested lists, parsed ordered-list start values, reference-link scope, and semantic fenced or indented code. Top-level thematic breaks render as dividers. Streaming lists deliberately remain on the existing prose path until completion so progressive word reveal is unchanged. Extraction is capped at 20 KB, 100 total items, and six nesting levels; unsupported or over-limit input falls back to the existing prose renderer. This PR does not change `MEDIA:` handling or the wire protocol. ## User Impact iOS conversations now preserve the structure of Markdown lists and thematic breaks. Numbering, nesting, task state, code blocks, and marker alignment remain readable at narrow widths, in light and dark appearance, and with accessibility text sizes. ## Evidence Visual proof was captured on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator running iOS 26.5. Before the fix, the issue reproduction collapses list markers and line structure; after the fix, it renders as a native ordered list with nested/task content and a divider. Screenshots are attached below. Exact-head validation at `642742733c9af6faf9800cfed4b77a5c4a1555c1`: - `swift test` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: 1,030 tests across 85 suites passed. - `swift test --filter ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests`: 91 tests passed after the final rebase. - iOS package test on iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5: 92 tests passed. - App-level `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`: 26 tests passed across light, dark, and accessibility text configurations at a 320-point width, including ordered items 9 and 10. - SwiftFormat 0.62.1: clean for all five changed files. - SwiftLint 0.65.0: zero violations for all five changed files. - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: clean. - Repository `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`: no accepted or actionable findings; patch assessed correct with 0.89 confidence. The global typography guard still reports unrelated existing offenders on the tested base; none are in the changed files. The focused app render smoke and changed-file formatting/lint gates are green. This PR is AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation, understand its parsing, fallback, streaming, and rendering behavior, and ran the validation above. ### Before ![Before: Markdown list flattened into prose](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metaforismo/openclaw/7fae6dda9d4165f8973c87388fd42f9bd26d3793/before.png) ### After ![After: native ordered, nested, and task list with thematic divider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metaforismo/openclaw/7fae6dda9d4165f8973c87388fd42f9bd26d3793/after.png)
